items.prompt:
Text A: 'Cats sleep a lot during the day. They are active at night.'
Text B: 'Cats have sharp claws that help them climb trees.'

What do both texts tell you about cats?
items.answer: Both texts are about cats, but they each share different facts. Both agree that cats are being described as animals with special traits.

steps: Text A talks about when cats sleep and when they are active.
Text B talks about cats' claws and climbing.
Both texts are describing characteristics of cats.
Both agree that cats have special traits that help them live their lives.

items.prompt:
Text A: 'Elephants are the largest land animals. They use their long trunks to pick up food and drink water.'
Text B: 'Elephants live in groups called herds. The oldest female leads the group.'

Name one fact from Text A that is NOT in Text B.
items.answer: Text A says elephants use their trunks to pick up food and drink water. This fact is not in Text B.

steps: Read Text A: largest land animal, use trunks to eat and drink.
Read Text B: live in herds, oldest female leads.
Is the trunk mentioned in Text B? No.
The trunk fact is only in Text A.

items.prompt:
Text A: 'Apples grow on trees. They can be red, yellow, or green.'
Text B: 'Apples are healthy to eat. They have vitamins and fiber.'

What is the same about both passages?
items.answer: Both passages are about apples. Both agree that apples exist and share information about them, though they focus on different things.

steps: Text A is about what apples look like and where they grow.
Text B is about why apples are healthy.
Both texts share the topic: apples.
The topic is the same even though the details are different.

items.prompt:
Text A: 'Sharks live in the ocean. They have sharp teeth to catch fish.'
Text B: 'Sharks have been on Earth for millions of years. They are one of the oldest creatures alive.'

Name one fact that is only in Text B.
items.answer: Text B says sharks have been on Earth for millions of years and are one of the oldest creatures alive. This is not mentioned in Text A.

steps: Text A says: sharks live in ocean, have sharp teeth.
Text B says: sharks are millions of years old, one of oldest creatures.
Is the age fact in Text A? No.
The fact about sharks being ancient is only in Text B.

items.prompt:
Text A: 'Penguins live in very cold places like Antarctica. They have black and white feathers.'
Text B: 'Penguins cannot fly, but they are excellent swimmers. They use their wings like flippers.'

What does Text A say about penguins? What does Text B say?
items.answer: Text A says penguins live in cold places and have black and white feathers. Text B says penguins cannot fly but are good swimmers and use their wings like flippers.

steps: Text A: home (cold places, Antarctica) and appearance (black and white feathers).
Text B: movement (cannot fly, swim well, wings as flippers).
Text A tells us where penguins live and what they look like.
Text B tells us how penguins move.

items.prompt:
Text A: 'The sun is a star. It is very far away from Earth.'
Text B: 'The sun rises in the east each morning. It sets in the west each evening.'

Do both texts agree that the sun is important? Find evidence.
items.answer: Both texts show the sun is important. Text A shows it by saying the sun is a star that is very far away, suggesting its size and distance matter. Text B shows it by describing how the sun rises and sets each day, marking our daily time.

steps: Text A: sun is a star, very far away. It is significant because of its size/distance.
Text B: sun marks morning and evening. People notice it daily.
Both texts describe the sun as something notable and worth knowing about.
They agree the sun is important, just from different angles.

items.prompt:
Text A: 'Rain forests are full of tall trees and many plants. They are found in warm, wet places.'
Text B: 'Rain forests are home to more kinds of animals than any other place on Earth.'

What one fact does only Text A tell you about rain forests?
items.answer: Only Text A tells us that rain forests are found in warm, wet places.

steps: Text A: tall trees, many plants, found in warm and wet places.
Text B: home to more animal kinds than anywhere else.
Is the 'warm and wet' fact in Text B? No.
The location and climate detail is only in Text A.

items.prompt:
Text A: 'Spiders have eight legs. They spin webs made of silk.'
Text B: 'Spiders are not insects. Insects have six legs, but spiders have eight.'

What fact appears in BOTH texts?
items.answer: Both texts say that spiders have eight legs.

steps: Text A says: eight legs, spin webs.
Text B says: not insects, insects have six legs, spiders have eight.
Is 'eight legs' in both? Yes.
Both texts mention that spiders have eight legs.

items.prompt:
Text A: 'Carrots grow underground. Farmers pull them out of the soil when they are ready.'
Text B: 'Carrots are orange vegetables. They are full of vitamins that help your eyes.'

What does Text A focus on? What does Text B focus on?
items.answer: Text A focuses on how carrots grow and how they are harvested. Text B focuses on what carrots look like and why they are healthy to eat.

steps: Text A: growing underground, being pulled out by farmers.
Text B: orange color, vitamins, good for eyes.
Text A is about where carrots come from (growing and harvesting).
Text B is about what carrots are like and what they do for your body.

items.prompt:
Text A: 'Ants live in large groups called colonies. Each ant has a special job.'
Text B: 'Ants are very strong for their size. They can carry objects much heavier than themselves.'

Name one way the texts are different.
items.answer: Text A is about how ants live together in groups with jobs, while Text B is about how strong ants are. The texts are different because Text A focuses on ant social life and Text B focuses on ant physical strength.

steps: Text A: colonies, special jobs. Topic: ant social structure.
Text B: very strong, carry heavy objects. Topic: ant physical ability.
Different topics: social life vs. physical strength.
The texts cover different facts about ants.

items.prompt:
Text A: 'The moon orbits Earth. It takes about 30 days to go all the way around.'
Text B: 'The moon lights up the night sky. It reflects light from the sun.'

Name one fact only in Text A and one fact only in Text B.
items.answer: Only in Text A: the moon takes about 30 days to orbit Earth. Only in Text B: the moon reflects light from the sun.

steps: Text A: orbits Earth, takes 30 days.
Text B: lights up the night sky, reflects sunlight.
Only Text A: the 30-day orbit.
Only Text B: the moon reflects light from the sun.

items.prompt:
Text A: 'Owls hunt at night. Their large eyes help them see in the dark.'
Text B: 'Owls make a hooting sound. They are known for being quiet fliers.'

What is the same about both texts?
items.answer: Both texts are about owls and describe their special abilities. Both show that owls are well-suited for nighttime life.

steps: Text A: night hunters, large eyes for seeing in dark.
Text B: hooting sound, quiet fliers.
Both are about owls.
Both describe special owl abilities that relate to the night.

items.prompt:
Text A: 'Dolphins live in oceans and seas. They breathe air through a hole on top of their head.'
Text B: 'Dolphins are very smart animals. They communicate with each other using clicks and whistles.'

Name one fact from each text that you find most interesting.
items.answer: From Text A: dolphins breathe through a hole on top of their head. From Text B: dolphins communicate using clicks and whistles. (Answers may vary; any specific fact from each text is acceptable.)

steps: Read Text A and pick one fact: dolphins breathe through a hole on top of their head.
Read Text B and pick one fact: they communicate with clicks and whistles.
Make sure you pick one from each text.
Any specific fact named from each text is a correct answer.

items.prompt:
Text A: 'Ladybugs are red with black spots. They are a type of beetle.'
Text B: 'Ladybugs eat tiny insects called aphids that destroy plants. Farmers love ladybugs.'

What does Text A tell you about what ladybugs LOOK like? What does Text B tell you about what ladybugs DO?
items.answer: Text A tells us ladybugs are red with black spots and are a type of beetle (appearance). Text B tells us ladybugs eat aphids that harm plants, and farmers appreciate them (behavior and usefulness).

steps: Text A = appearance: red with black spots, type of beetle.
Text B = behavior/use: eat aphids, help farmers.
Text A answers 'what do ladybugs look like?'
Text B answers 'what do ladybugs do?'

items.prompt:
Text A: 'Snow is water that has frozen into tiny ice crystals. It falls when the air is very cold.'
Text B: 'Heavy snow can make roads slippery. People use salt and sand to make roads safer.'

Text A is about what snow IS. What is Text B about?
items.answer: Text B is about what happens when there is heavy snow and how people deal with it. Text B is about the effects of snow and human responses to it.

steps: Text A explains what snow is (frozen water) and when it forms (cold air).
Text B explains a problem snow causes (slippery roads) and the solution (salt and sand).
Text A is about what snow IS.
Text B is about what snow DOES and how people respond.
